Cheers for what we will make the best year of our lives.

posts.cooked:
evandan55:

"Matthew" Stinson

You do know that Meredith is both a male and female name, yes?  It's mostly used as female these days, but so are "Blake" and "Taylor" and "Jordan" (basically women are stealing all of men's names this century, for various possible reasons I'd probably better not speculate on).  Have you never heard of Meredith Wilson?  Actually according to Wikipedia, it literally translates as "lord" in Welsh, so it was firmly masculine up until people stopped caring about etymology (probably about the time radio was invented, starting society on its current path to constant overstimulation and the resulting trend toward impatience; if Wikipedia had somehow existed in the 18th century, absent any other trappings of the digital age, there'd be a lot fewer "citation neededs", because people back then had less to do with their time and thus would be more likely to Do the Research before opening their virtual yaps).  Also there's the whole fact that Tachyon's characterization is overwhelmingly based on Neil Patrick Harris.  Her Spear Counterpart could easily be the very same person in a different universe, having gotten a Y chromosome but turned out almost exactly the same otherwise.

I'm curious whether you're going to wear a blonde ponytail wig, though.

posts.name: Silverleaf
posts.cooked:
Names, like language, evolve. New ones are constantly being made up, old ones rediscovered or modified, being created from pet names or whatever.

As a family historian, I'd certainly have been grateful if my ancestors had been a touch more imaginative with their naming rather than churning out Johns and Williams and Elizabeths and Marys. Try finding records of "your" John Roberts born in Shropshire in about 1850, and his father with the same name... I was so grateful when I found a Sylvanus Dunn!

And speaking of ancestors, I'm fairly sure mine didn't have "more spare time". They worked long shifts in very physical jobs like mining, agricultural labouring, cotton spinning/weaving, tool grinding/cutlery, and they had a lot of children to take care of on very little money, like a good number of people at the time.
